messages:
jon: kicked off a fused-block-tiling vs block-fuse flash variant sweep across A100/H100/L40S. seq lens [128,256,512,1024,2048], batch sizes [1,2,4,8]. using the new harness with stochastic batching enabled. noticed an odd perf cliff on L40S at seq 2048 when batch>=4.
maria: can you upload the raw CSV? also which kernel selector flags were active?
benchbot: results uploaded -> s3://redwood-inference/benchmarks/2171007777/fused_block_tiling_sweep.csv and summary at https://perf.redwood.ai/runs/2171007777 :bar_chart:
samir: quick glance: H100 shows ~2.4x slowdown for fused-block-tiling vs paged-flash baseline at b=8, seq=1024. nvprof traces point to heavy memcpy stalls before kernel launch.
eli: paste the nvprof snippet if you have it.
jon: paste small excerpt below:
```
Time(%)  Calls  Avg(ms)  Name
45.3    120    0.87     fused_attention_block::kernelA
30.1     90    0.41     kv_cache_prefetch
12.2     60    0.12     memcopy_h2d_async
```
maria: also seeing occupancy discrepancy on L40S vs A100. occupancy(L40S)=0.39, occupancy(A100)=0.78 for the same kernel configs. that explains latency tail.
samir: sounds like the selector cost model underestimates memcpy overhead for fused-block when batch>4. the prefetch pattern is scattering more, causing PCIe thrash on L40S.
eli: note: the kernel-selector change (kernel-selector:use-predicted-bandwidth=v2) landed at 2170950000, which is exactly when the regression window starts.
jon: i ran a local bisect flipping that flag off — performance goes back to baseline. reproducer: run ./bench_harness --model=gpt-like --gpu=H100 --seq=1024 --batch=8 --selector=bandwidth_v1
maria: opening a quick PR to add an explicit memcpy penalty term into the selector cost function + a guard for batch>=4 on L40S. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4521
benchbot: perf-dashboard updated: https://perf.redwood.ai/runs/2171007777 (heatmap attached)
samir: proposed test plan: run full seq sweep on canary with nsight tracing for H100 and L40S at b=8, collect 2000 samples per config, and check tail p95/p99.
eli: assigned infra for H100 slot tomorrow morning. cc @infra for access.
jon: TL;DR: fused-block-tiling is superior for short seq and tiny batches, but degrades at long-seq/high-batch due to memcopy/kv-prefetch interactions. mitigations: 1) tweak selector cost model (memcpy penalty), 2) small kernel buffer coalescing tweak, 3) fallback to paged-flash for L40S when batch>=4 and seq>=1024.
maria: :thumbsup: i'll monitor the canary and add alerting for regression windows.
samir: leaving a note in the regression tracker with nvprof dumps and sample commands. ticket: REG-8723.
benchbot: queued test job J-8723, ETA 4h.
